_comment: Hook wiring. Delete this _comment key before use —
it is documentation, not configuration, and some tools reject unknown keys.
Rules are not delivered by a hook: Claude Code loads each .claude/rules/*.md when
the agent first touches a file its paths: header names, and Cursor reads the .mdc
projection. Hooks speak only at moments
nothing else serves. capture-at-write.sh fires on Edit and Write of a rule,
decision record or framework document. The Bash matcher carries four hooks for
moments no file path marks: merging a plan, committing a change to the rules or
framework, creating a branch in the main checkout, and committing or pushing in a
public project. The first two are
narrowed to their command shape by an `if`; public-exposure-check.sh has two
triggers, so it has no `if` and matches commit and push itself. Each re-checks the
command itself. Every hook replies through .tropis/hooks/hook-reply.sh, the one
shape both tools pass to the agent.
Everything else is project-specific and belongs here only when the project needs
it. What the two source projects added, as examples of the kind of thing that
goes here rather than as defaults to copy:
- a permissions.deny list naming credential files, so a read is refused rather
than merely discouraged;
- a second Read hook guarding those same files, because a deny list and a guard
fail in different ways;
- a Bash hook checking commit commands against the commit format.
Order matters within a matcher: hooks run in sequence, and a guard that blocks
should run before one that only adds context.
